stemMd: Two solid objects have identical front silhouettes but different depths. Which conclusion is justified from the front silhouettes alone?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They need not have equal volumes.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Neither can be drawn in a side view.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They must be the same object.

explanationMd: A front projection removes depth information. Solids can share a silhouette while extending different distances backwards, so volume cannot generally be inferred from that view alone.

distractorRationale.b: Depth differences can change volume without changing front view.
distractorRationale.d: One projection does not uniquely determine a solid.
distractorRationale.e: The front silhouettes show the same height profile.
